title: Safe Data Structures
story: Every production codebase eventually accumulates 'validation utility' functions scattered across 20 files. A centralized library of safe types eliminates this sprawl — validate once, use everywhere.
why: A library of small, focused invariant types replaces ad-hoc validation with type-guaranteed safety across the entire codebase.
analogy: A safe type library is like a set of calibrated measuring cups — each guarantees an exact amount. You don't need to re-measure every time you pour.
try_it: Add a `ValidUrl` type with an invariant that checks for `http://` or `https://` at the start. Then add a `ValidCreditCard` type with an invariant checking that the string length is exactly 16. Build a checkout function that takes both.
tips: Start with small, single-purpose types — each with exactly one invariant
Compose them in function signatures — the safety compounds
Keep your safe types in a shared module — `safe_types.xi` — so every module can import them
common_mistakes: Making types too broad — `ValidString` is meaningless; `NonEmptyStr` is precise
Re-validating inside functions that receive safe types — the type already did the work
Creating a safe type but accepting raw strings in most functions — commit to using the safe type consistently
